### 2026-10-06 – I understand how net labels work in kikad work now. Following the github week 1 guide, I thought that after drawing the esp they intentionally provided "hints" by not drawing the wiring that routed to

**1.5h**

I understand how net labels work in kikad work now. Following the github week 1 guide, I thought that after drawing the esp they intentionally provided "hints" by not drawing the wiring that routed to the ESP. Eventually as i drawed using wires it got really confusing and i was struggling alot. Following a google search i found out that net labels of the same name establish a connection. Although now re-reading the guide I understand that it told me so in "The net labels tell the schematic that those parts need to be connected without having to draw wires all over", I read and didn't understand it before. Wasted lots of time on this having to restart, and lookout timelapse app for some reason didnt capture my desktop and only my browser so it didnt see my kicad progress which sucks. So this will be a manual entry instead of a timelapse. And i had to use the undo and redo function to take the screenshots of during the mistake and when i restarted cuz i never knew timelapse would act up on me

tldr: wasted a lot of time because i didnt realise the function of net labels, now i have to restart

### 2026-10-07 – I followed the PCB routing process. However, it initially gave me warnings and errors.

**2.5h**

I followed the PCB routing process. However, it initially gave me warnings and errors.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 143032](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/bc5b71c7184801637245d87299a62fd07bef7c31a870515747f766a3e4a83074.png)

I eventually fixed the errors by going back and making sure the net labels were named correctly, specifically spaces in DHT11 DATA  that caused the errors and also one instance where my SCL and SDA was flipped. Now i have 0 errors and some warnings. The warnings are about some sort of missing padding or whatever. But i can't figure out why this happens. At the moment though I've been able to continue through the tutorial so i guess ill leave it until i see it pop up again since it only showed once when i imported the pcb in the editor.
For the boundary, i watched https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=upaHLpd6N4o and  and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=muq3DlWbwh8

I then started routing.
![5f72aaa0-d229-4624-8a0c-827dd9a3110d](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/6457c35a48c06249a6685dcb714dec7c33e194a674df91cf20946bc6663059c2.png)
It was really ugly and took a while to find the areas i had to press X on, because all contact points were highlighted blue so i just clicked on all of them and tried routing but there would be no endpoint. Realised that the points with a blue line meant unrouted and the ones without the blue lines meant it didnt need to be routed. Also figured out that F.Cu was the front and B.Cu was the back, so that helped with a lot of routing blockades. Probably could have stuck with F.Cu only if i placed everything in a better position but i don't know how so i just took the easy way out.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/82b41daad4897291e774e042331db22a26b51e071792f6f11a4bbdf9169dbb27.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/d82ab70a7fb4740634b059e24c4c5cefda3e127be14bb59ae31208e12f3656de.png)

Finished routing. Searched up what a GND ground pour was. So it removes the need for wiring to ground and makes the circuit look cleaner. So i removed all the GND points (5), watched https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DNTgrTukltw and started doing it

result:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/55b5859f1f386a8812d750d703bb82c5cf602063cb10dd8e8d55b0e01e460dec.png)

tldr: Fixed routing errors, routed, learnt about layers and added GND ground pour

next time: Figure out how to add a bh1750 light sensor module since KiCad doesn't have it, so will start learning how to make it and do footprints for it and stuff. And then check for errors.

### 2026-10-08 – Faced an issue with the "thermal relief connection".

**3.5h**

Faced an issue with the "thermal relief connection".
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/ee8a138dbaca3b75f296ce7e7b6b6d62fc4df874ce863b294331793d94e66e8e.png)

Fixed it by rerouting a path. Also added rounded corners to the perimeter of the rectangle. I want to add a BH1750 light sensor before I continue. Using https://dfimg.dfrobot.com/wiki/17472/SEN0097_bh1750-light-intensity-sensor_datasheet_1.0.pdf,
I saw that it has 6 pins. I did a search and found out this was for the bare chip, not the breakout module. So i have to restart.
Using https://pinoutdb.org/en/component/bh1750, I

Actually, i think my project will be better if i use a AT42QT1010 touch capacitor. It will let the thing react when i touch it, which i think is better than a light intensity sensor as its more reactive. Since thheres a funding limit, ill probably just add this and then do the footprints etc before gathering a BOM and seeing how many more modules I can add.
referenced https://core-electronics.com.au/capacitive-touch-breakout-at42qt1010.html
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/4972f2cbcb0def0d558d9fd0f48f6938702c9bf9c285895b903bb12bbc42c582.png)

I'm thinking that as part of the process to change mine so it isnt identical to the guide, I want to eventually integrate very simple AI of some form. Like a simple personality system and memory system that lets it remmber my name and stuff like how I handled it. It may wander around the screen maybe. Like if i pet it when its "scared" it may gradually associate touch with comfort, which could be made through the touch capacitor I mentioned before. Not sure how i'll do the ai stuff though. Probably have to use cloud service but i did a search and the esp has wifi i believe. Will only do this if i have time and am bothered to learn this stuff though, only an idea.

I figured out how to connect the new module i made in the schematic to the ESP through net labels

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/144446a1d5f2e6077ced0af0deed0d8a3e24eb60e3eac73fc8f49c6fb0d8b6e9.png)

I read https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/at42qt101x-capacitive-touch-breakout-hookup-guide/hardware and found out what PAD is. Don't think ill use it to keep it simple

I read https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/at42qt1010-capacitive-touch-breakout-hookup-guide/hardw  to learn what the LED header does. Skipping it because i don't need a light and it adds extra  complexity

On google, i searched up what the difference between vvertical and horizontal was like in Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm:PinHeader_1x04_P2.54mm_Vertical
Previously ithought that both horizontal and vertical were just like orientation perpendicular to the board, but now i realised that horizontal means its parralel which isnt what i want

Also now i realise how assigning footprints work. Before i didn't understand, but now i know that it creates holes in the PCB at 2.54mm apart, which is the same as the distance between holes on my touch module

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/93082833862a7c08f06a3802016e29906b81036134b98bd105e89544d64fe520.png)

im getting these warnings when i try to update my pcb with the touch capacitor.

I found out why. The care package had a c6 footprint whilst i needed a c3. They gave the wrong one, so i had to go to slack and find the link that someone posted (https://github.com/Seeed-Studio/OPL_Kicad_Library/blob/master/Seeed%20Studio%20XIAO%20Series%20Library/XIAO-ESP32-C3-SMD.kicad_mod)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/5f207b220d97477ada4f7961ff01f8519cb8b6a67130c6869683903572b5af94.png)

It works now. I will route the touch thing.

I am facing issues again. My schematic symbol has 22 pins, but the DIP footprint only has 14 pads.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/l46XmsBE41tdBulSbMyXAL2SgBHJAIib/a7483fd004639fd7cc4a94a0d276ef1e43de832c8e25092dbe7d87397d113fc8.png)

changed it to New_XIAO_Series_Footprints:XIAO-ESP32-C3-DIP-SMD. 0 errors and 0 warnings. But I now have extra pads compared to the tutorial and 8 extra SMDS. I don't know why this discrepancy exists but many people faced it as far as i can see in slack. I think i will keep this for now. Design rule checker shows no wrong. But with these extra paddings it means if i solder onto it then the module won't lie flat... I will look into this further in the next session.

tldr: Fixed a thermal relief issue by rerouting a trace and rounded the PCB corners.Added an AT42QT1010 capacitive touch sensor instead of a light sensor and routed it. troubleshot several PCB errors caused by incorrect ESP32-C3 footprints and pad mismatches. Design checker shows no warnings.

next session: look into how to remove the need for the SMD pads to go back to the guide's 14.
